test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: As per National Mineral Inventory on 01.04.2020, which Indian State hosts the country's 90% diamond?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **National Mineral Inventory** data as of **01.04.2020**, the state of **Madhya Pradesh** is the primary repository of diamond resources in India.
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** accounts for approximately **90.18%** of the total diamond resources in the country, making it the leading state in this sector.
 
• The **Panna** district in **Madhya Pradesh** is world-renowned for its diamond deposits and is the only place in India where organized diamond mining occurs.
 
• The **Majhgawan** diamond mine, located in **Panna**, is the only mechanized diamond mine in the country and is operated by the **National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC)**.
 
• The total resources of diamond in India are estimated at about **31.83 million carats**, out of which the majority is concentrated in the **Vindhyan system** of **Madhya Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geological Formations**: In India, diamonds are generally found in three types of geological settings: **Kimberlite pipes** (primary source), **Conglomerate beds**, and **Alluvial gravels**.
 
• **Distribution in Other States**: Apart from **Madhya Pradesh**, other states that host diamond resources include **Andhra Pradesh** (approximately **5.72%**) and **Chhattisgarh** (approximately **4.09%**).
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**: Historically, this state was famous for its **Golkonda diamonds**. Regions such as **Anantapur**, **Kurnool**, and the **Krishna River basin** have recorded significant diamond occurrences in the past, including the discovery of the legendary **Koh-i-Noor**.
 
• **Chhattisgarh**: Resources are primarily located in the **Behraidih-Tokapal** area in the **Bastar** and **Raipur** districts.
 
• **Industrial Use**: Diamonds that are not of gem quality are known as **bort** or **industrial diamonds**. Because of their extreme **hardness** (10 on the Mohs scale), they are used extensively in **drilling bits**, **glass cutting**, and **polishing** other gemstones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Resource Classification**: As per the **UNFC (United Nations Framework Classification)** adopted by the **Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM)**, mineral resources are divided into **Reserves** (proven and probable) and **Remaining Resources**.
 
• For diamonds in India, as of **2020**, the **Reserves** stand at only about **0.95 million carats**, while the **Remaining Resources** are estimated at **30.87 million carats**.
 
• **Chemical Composition**: A diamond is a solid form of the element **Carbon** with its atoms arranged in a crystal structure called **diamond cubic**. It has the highest **thermal conductivity** of any natural material.
 
• **Statutory Body**: The **Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM)**, established in **1948**, is responsible for the compilation of the **National Mineral Inventory** and ensures the scientific development of mineral resources in **India**.
